patient_summary:
Hello there, you're doing well! I'm glad to see you're feeling better and going to the gym more. You've lost a bit of weight, but that's okay. You're still eating and going to the bathroom normally. You're also feeling good and have a lot of energy. 

You're taking some medicines to help you. You take a multivitamin every day, aspirin once a day, Lupron every three months, Flomax 0.4 mg once a day, and Warfarin 2.5 mg twice a day. 

You told me you've had atrial fibrillation, which is a type of heart problem. You're doing well overall, but if you have any of these symptoms, you should call us right away:
- Fever or chills
- Nausea or vomiting
- Any change in your bowel or bladder habits

If you have any questions or need help, just let us know. We're here to help you stay healthy.
caregiver_checklist: Check aspirin dose and time with the patient.
Watch for fever, chills, nausea, or vomiting.
Call if atrial fibrillation symptoms persist or worsen.
Check Warfarin 2.5 mg dose and time.
Watch for signs of bleeding or bruising.
Call if Warfarin INR levels are outside the target range.
Schedule EKG if atrial fibrillation persists.
Check for any new or worsening symptoms.
Call if any new symptoms appear or worsen.
Ensure aspirin is 0.4 mg and taken q.d.
Ensure Warfarin is 2.5 mg and taken q.d.
child_explanation: You have a health problem called atrial fibrillation. It's like a small glitch in your heart's rhythm. You're doing well and the grown-ups and doctors are taking good care of you. You're exercising more and have lost some weight. You feel good and have lots of energy. The doctors gave you a few medicines to help. They're watching you closely to make sure you stay healthy.
source_text: CHIEF COMPLAINT: , MGUS.,HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:,  This is an extremely pleasant 86-year-old gentleman, who I follow for his MGUS.  I initially saw him for thrombocytopenia when his ANC was 1300.  A bone marrow biopsy was obtained.  Interestingly enough, at the time of his bone marrow biopsy, his hemoglobin was 13.0 and his white blood cell count was 6.5 with a platelet count of 484,000.  His bone marrow biopsy showed a normal cellular bone marrow; however, there were 10% plasma cells and we proceeded with the workup for a plasma cell dyscrasia.  All his tests came back as consistent with an MGUS.,Overall, he is doing well.  Since I last saw him, he tells me that he has had onset of atrial fibrillation.  He has now started going to the gym two times per week, and has lost over 10 pounds.  He has a good energy level and his ECOG performance status is 0.  He denies any fever, chills, or night sweats.  No lymphadenopathy.  No nausea or vomiting.  No change in bowel or bladder habits.,CURRENT MEDICATIONS: , Multivitamin q.d., aspirin one tablet q.d., Lupron q. three months, Flomax  0.4 mg q.d., and Warfarin 2.5 mg q.d.,ALLERGIES:  ,No known drug allergies.,REVIEW OF SYSTEMS: , As per the HPI, otherwise negative.,PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:,1.  He is status post left inguinal hernia repair.,2.  Prostate cancer diagnosed in December 2004, which was a Gleason 3+4.  He is now receiving Lupron.,SOCIAL HISTORY: , He has a very remote history of tobacco use.  He has one to two alcoholic drinks per day.
